repo.description:
## Summary

Every procedure in `networkRouter` is a plain `protectedProcedure` with no permission check (`routers/network.ts`). Any authenticated user, including members with zero docker-related permissions, can create, inspect, recreate, import and delete docker networks.

Verified live: a member account with no permissions called `network.create` and a docker network was created on the server.

## Details

All of these are `protectedProcedure` only:

- `network.all`, `network.networksToSync`, `network.one`, `network.inspect` - read/list
- `network.create`, `network.import`, `network.recreate`, `network.resync` - create/modify
- `network.remove` - delete

Members have no `docker` permission at all (`access-control.ts:179` - `docker: []`), yet all of the above succeed.

`one`, `inspect`, `recreate`, `resync` and `remove` do check `network.organizationId === activeOrganizationId`, so they are limited to the caller's org. `create` and `import` accept an optional `serverId` that is never validated against the org (`network.ts:52-66, 76-98`), and `createNetwork` stores it verbatim then calls `getRemoteDocker(serverId)` (`services/network.ts:289,321`). Within the org this is trivially exploitable since `network.all` returns every serverId to any member. Pointing at another organization's server requires knowing its id (not guessable, but obtainable through other data leaks); the lack of an ownership check is verifiable by targeting a server in an organization the caller controls.

Impact inside the org: a member can delete `dokploy-network` or any service network, which cuts connectivity for every app on it (instance-wide denial of service), or create networks with attacker-chosen driver/IPAM options.

## Steps to reproduce

Tested on a self-hosted install (v0.30.6).

As a member with no permissions:

```
POST /api/trpc/network.create?batch=1
{"0":{"json":{"name":"pwned-net"}}}
```

`docker network ls` on the host shows `pwned-net` (verified: the member's call created the network on the host). `network.all` also returns the full network list to the member, and `network.remove` with the id deletes it again. All calls succeed for a member with no docker permissions.
repo.summary: Missing authorization on all network.* endpoints (Member -> create/delete docker networks on org servers, cross-org access via serverId)
